newsitem.title: UK: FX in Europe - Dlr stalls as Buba rate fears ebb.
newsitem.headline: FX in Europe - Dlr stalls as Buba rate fears ebb.

text.p: Calm descended on the currency markets in Europe on Tuesday and the dollar ended little changed against the German mark as concern about an imminent Bundesbank rate rise eased and fears of stock market turbulence ebbed.

A fixed and unchanged securities repurchase rate at the weekly Bundesbank market tender and news of slower M3 money supply growth in July lengthened the odds on a rate rise at the central bank's policy-making making on Thursday, analysts said.
This followed comments from Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp late Monday saying that a rate rise now risked severely damaging the already fragile German economy.
The International Monetary Fund and the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development also added their voices and cautioned against the need for higher German rates.

"The real money managers, and not necessarily the short-term players, still believe dollar/mark is more likely to continue upwards than turn down," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

"The Bundesbank has created more of a two-way market, however. While there's no compelling economic reason for a rate rise just yet they have let the market know that continued mark weakness would change their assessment of the situation."

At 1525 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.8395/00 compared with 1.8365/75 late Monday. Traders said stiff resistance to moves above 1.84 was detected, although rumours that a European central bank was selling at that level could not be confirmed.
Chartists said strong resistance to dollar gains was expected about 1.8420, where a falling trendline from early August currently cuts in.

Otherwise, the markets displayed a desire to trade established ranges for a while. The Federal Reserve's policy- making Open Market Committee also met and helped crimp volumes, but few expected any changes in interest rates there either.

"Both events (Fed and Bundesbank meetings) are non-events as far as interest rate rises are concerned but they add to the dollar's consolidation mode," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago. "It's slightly firmer because the unchanged repo and the M3 figure gave the market reason to sell marks."
The Bundesbank said July M3 grew an annualised 5.7 percent versus the fourth quarter of 1996, down from 6.4 in June.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast an M3 growth rate of 6.3 percent.
The OECD said in a report on Germany that it saw no reason for a change in German monetary policy through 1998.

Earlier, IMF managing director Michel Camdessus urged the Bundesbank to consider any pressure to raise rates calmly and said dollar levels were justified, even if the speed of its recent gains were alarming.

Apart from the Bundesbank meeting Thursday, traders will eye German Ifo Institute's business sentiment index, due on Wednesday. This is expected to rise from 96.0 in June to between 96.4 and 97.2 and July.
Easing German rate fears, meantime, weighed slightly on the mark against its neighbouring European currencies.
